Messages.Body:
Hi,

i have qrules question i amnot sure about. if a Vampire with a raptor blocks an Action and Plays obedience does the opposing Player gets the -1 handsize and has to discard?

Raptor

Retainer] Retainer

[Animalism] Animalism

[2 Blood]

Animal with 1 life.
[ani] The minion with this retainer gets +1 intercept.
[ANI] As above, and when the minion with this retainer is in combat, the opposing minion's controller gets -1 hand size.

Obedience

[Reaction] Reaction

[Dominate] Dominate

Only usable when this reacting vampire is about to enter combat with an acting younger vampire.
[dom] Untap the acting vampire, do not tap this reacting vampire, and end the current action (and combat). The acting vampire cannot attempt the same action this turn.
[DOM] As above, but do not untap the acting vampire.

since obedience says "end the Action (and combat)" i thought there has to be a combat at some point otherwise you couldnt end it. but i am not sure.

Thanks in advance!

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> gameover wrote:
> i have qrules question i amnot sure about. if a Vampire with a raptor blocks an Action and Plays obedience does the opposing Player gets the -1 handsize and has to discard?
>
No.

Obedience is played before combat happens ("about to enter combat"), and terminates the action and the combat that would be about to start. But the vampires never actually get into combat, so Raptor's text never activates.

Messages.Author: TwoRazorReign
Messages.Body: Is there a reason why the card mentions to end combat? It seems like it should state that the action ends but combat does not occur.

Messages.Author: TwoRazorReign
Messages.Body:
Here's my guess:

The change to the current text on Obedience happened in Camarilla edition. Back then, tapping from the result of a block and entering combat was one step, so a blocking minion entered combat and tapped at the same time. Since then, tapping resulting from a block was given it's own discreet step before entering combat. Obedience was never changed to reflect this. Perhaps it was an oversight?

Complete Rules Reference v. 3.1 (1998):

"b. Tap Blocking Minion and either Resolve Combat [6.2.3] or allow
Diablerie [6.5.2], as appropriate."

Detailed Play Summary:

"b. Tap blocking minion.
c. If the acting minion was acting from the ready region, he enters combat with the blocking minion (VI)
d. If the acting minion was acting from torpor and the blocking minion is a vampire, the blocker may diablerize the acting vampire. (VIII) [6.5.2]"
